svg.title: A recorded 64-second run of the station on the board, in three terminal panes: the Linux dashboard on CPU 2, the acquisition and analysis logs of CPUs 0 and 1, and the hart 4 console. It shows the roll call, normal operation at about 1000 frames per second, a trip on bad frames and a reset, a trip on a missed deadline after the analysis process is frozen and a reset, and the closing summary.

g.text: [station] DISARM from ARMED: 467 status, 94 windows, 1 deadline misses, 0 seq mismatches, 2 trips
Core 1 speaks
Linux CPU 0 sends HELLO; hart 4 prints it on its UART and answers with its own tick count.
All three Linux cores heard
CPU 2 is the third; hart 4 reports that it has heard harts 1, 2 and 3.
Core 4 speaks
Hart 4 sends one message of its own to Linux, and the listener on Linux prints it.
The station starts
Acquisition on CPU 0, analysis on CPU 1, telemetry on CPU 2; hart 4 arms with its limits.
Normal operation
About 1000 frames per second, no bad frames; hart 4 prints a window line every tenth window.
Fault A: corrupt frames
The operator asks for CRC faults; the fabric corrupts one frame in every injection run.
A run ends without a stall
The 5000-slot run ended on 4999 UIO events; the last frame was taken from its descriptor and the injection runs start at once.
Trip on bad frames
Hart 4 sees 5 bad frames in a window, aborts the source and shows SAFE on all three consoles.
Operator reset
The reset travels CPU 2, CPU 1 and RPMsg to hart 4; the station is armed and running again.
Fault B: the analysis process hangs
After kill -STOP on CPU 1, no message reaches hart 4 for 500 ms: ALARM, then a trip on DEADLINE.
The frozen process wakes up
After kill -CONT, CPU 1 receives the trip notice that hart 4 sent while it was frozen.
Second reset
The station resumes and runs normally to the end.
Summary
37,589 frames verified, 5 bad, 2 trips, 0 sequence mismatches; hart 4's own counts agree.
